grh_cb4234c7c23f751b7fe7.title: Portrait of Jenny
paragraphs: Struggling artist Eben Adams meets the mysterious Jennie in Central Park and discovers that each time she reappears she has aged years while almost no time has passed for him. Loving her transforms his work, and her portrait becomes the painting that finally gives his art life. Eben learns that Jennie belongs to another time and died in a New England storm, then races to the lighthouse where her fate is repeating. He reaches her but cannot defeat the great wave that takes her again. Years later, after Eben's own death, the story closes with the suggestion that the two have finally crossed time to reunite.

Other credited names include Bill Cairn as director, Howard Wiley as producer, and Milton Geiger as radio adaptor.
The surviving recording runs about 30 minutes. The broadcast is also associated with [[org|org.47c43e9eb0213c63|RCA]].
This version presents a radio version of [[work|work.sdp.film.72deaf017139b322|Portrait of Jenny]]. Robert Nathan is credited as author and Milton Geiger adapted it for radio.

grh_cb32093fb6397815b042.title: The Chocolate Soldier
paragraphs: Nadina dreams of heroic romance and is engaged to the boastful soldier Alexius, but during wartime she hides Swiss officer Bumerli, a practical fugitive who carries chocolates instead of bullets and refuses to pretend that battle is glorious. When Bumerli later returns, the household's romantic posturing collapses and Nadina recognizes the difference between theatrical heroism and the man she actually loves. Bumerli reveals that he is the son of a wealthy Swiss hotel owner and asks for Nadina, who finally embraces her unlikely 'chocolate soldier' as her true hero.

grh_cb03c8a1a5c758554589.title: The Navy Hunts the Cgr 3070
paragraphs: The Coast Guard Reserve yacht CGR-3070 begins an ordinary coastal picket patrol searching for enemy submarines, but a severe Atlantic storm turns the mission into a survival ordeal. The small craft is battered, flooded and damaged, several men are injured, and a tow from a British destroyer later parts in heavy weather. With the radio failing and rescue attempts repeatedly missing them, the crew patches the boat, rations what remains and keeps sailing. A convoy is unable to take them off, but the men refuse to give up, and a patrol vessel finally finds them off the North Carolina coast. Every crewman walks ashore, embarrassed only that they never actually sighted a German submarine.
